subject: Inference cost review & next steps — PulseCare feature pricing
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@pulsecare.com>, Dennis O'Neal <dennis.oneal@pulsecare.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:05:00-04:00
Subject: Post-call recap — inference cost assumptions and next steps

Hi Sarah / Dennis — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have a shared starting point and a clear set of next steps. I’ve also attached a simple model (token_volume_model.xlsx) for transparency.

Summary of what I heard
- Target features: Symptom Checker (feature A) + Triage Assistant (feature B) as MVP.
- Expected traffic: ~20k user requests/day for Symptom Checker, ~8k requests/day for Triage -> ~28k QPS/day aggregated (production-like peak smoothing planned).
- Average prompt/response size we should budget for: 120 tokens input + 220 tokens output (avg conversation length) = ~340 tokens per request.
- Baseline forecast: 28k * 340 * 30 = ~285,600,000 tokens/month (~286M).

Business targets you mentioned
- Primary target: keep inference spend in the neighborhood of $40k–$60k/month during pilot.
- Stretch target: push unit cost to <$200 per 1M tokens if possible for committed volumes.
- CAC / payback: internal goal ~6–9 months payback on acquisition for the first cohort.

Initial cost math (back-of-envelope)
- If we price inference at $200 / 1M tokens: 286M tokens -> $57,200 / month (inference-only).
- Per-feature monthly inference cost (approx): Symptom Checker ~72M tokens -> $14,400; Triage ~214M tokens -> $42,800.
- If we can get to $150 / 1M tokens via quantized model + reserved capacity: 286M -> $42,900 / month.

Margin & unit economics notes
- Target gross margin on the feature: 65%+ (we used 70% as an internal goal). At $42k inference cost and target ARR per active account of $200k/year, payback timeline looks feasible; we’ll map per-account usage in the model.
- CAC payback sensitivity: if CAC is $30k and contribution margin is 60%, payback ~5 months at forecasted conversion ARPU.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) Rishi: share token model (attached) and a 3-scenario cost sheet (baseline / optimized quantized / reserved capacity). (attached)
2) Sarah: confirm whether 340 tokens/request is a fair average and whether any heavy-image attachments or long histories will change token assumptions.
3) Dennis / procurement: share target contract duration (pilot 3 months vs 6 months) and any specific PO or compliance flow.
4) Redwood: provide SOC2 + redlined SOW for procurement review (we’ll attach draft SOW).

If the $40k–$60k pilot budget is fixed we can present a tuned model that trades latency for lower cost (e.g., L2 quantization + 8-bit kernels, smaller candidate model for the triage fallback). Happy to jump on a 30m follow-up this week to run the three scenarios live.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194

From: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@pulsecare.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Dennis O'Neal <dennis.oneal@pulsecare.com>, procurement@pulsecare.com
Date: 2027-08-14T10:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — inference cost assumptions and next steps

Thanks Rishi — this is great, appreciate the clear math. A few clarifications from our side:
- Token assumptions: 340 avg looks right for symptomatic flows. We have occasional longer threads when clinicians jump in, but that’s ~5% of traffic.
- Volume check: the 20k/8k split is accurate for phase 1 in our midwest region; we may see +25% in Q4.
- Budget: procurement has conservatively carved out $45k/month for pilot, could stretch to $55k with exec sign-off.

Requests:
1) Can you produce a cost table for 3 scenarios: (A) standard hosted @ $/1M baseline, (B) optimized quantized with reserved nodes (assume 20% lower unit cost), (C) fallback hybrid where triage uses a cheaper distilled model for NPS < threshold?
2) Can you call out the impact to latency (p95) for the optimized scenario — we need <800ms p95 ideally.

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to start the pilot 9/20; procurement will need SOC2 docs and a draft SOW for initial review this week.

Sarah Tan
Head of Product Operations | PulseCare
sarah.tan@pulsecare.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@pulsecare.com>, Dennis O'Neal <dennis.oneal@pulsecare.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T12:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — inference cost assumptions and next steps

Thanks — agree on the three scenarios. Quick bullets while I assemble the sheet:
- Scenario A (baseline): $220 / 1M tokens (conservative list pricing) -> est $62.9k / month for 286M tokens. p95 latency (single-region hosted small fleet): ~400–700ms depending on concurrency.
- Scenario B (optimized): $175 / 1M tokens (8-bit quant + reserved capacity) -> est $50k / month. Expect p95 ~500–850ms; we’ll size for <800ms p95 for the triage path.
- Scenario C (hybrid): use a distilled 3B param fallback for lower-cost triage traffic; effective blended unit cost could be ~$140 / 1M tokens for the combined workload -> est $40k / month. Latency profile: triage fallback p95 <600ms, symptom checker on higher-capacity model p95 <750ms.

I’ve attached token_volume_model.xlsx (scenario tabs + per-feature rows) and a redline SOW (PulseCare_SOW_draft.pdf). I’ll also add a simple per-account ARR sheet to show CAC payback windows (6/9/12 month lines).

Can we do a 30m call tomorrow 11am PT to review the scenario sheet with your engineering lead? If that works I’ll send a calendared invite and include Monica (solutions engineering) who will run the latency sizing.

Rishi

Rishi / Sarah — procurement here. Quick checklist from our side for the pilot:
- Need SOC2 Type II report and evidence of encryption at rest + in transit.
- Please provide expected invoicing cadence and whether Redwood supports monthly or net-30 billing.
- If we move forward with reserved capacity, we require a 3-month minimum commitment for the pilot (with extension to 6 months if we scale).
- We’ll get PO ready but need the redlined SOW and an estimated not-to-exceed amount. With $45k/month budget the NTE for a 3-month pilot would be $135k.

Procurement contact: procurement@pulsecare.com
Dennis O'Neal
Director, Procurement | PulseCare

Dennis / team — appreciate the checklist. Quick replies inline: 
- SOC2 & compliance: attaching SOC2 summary link in Drive and we’ll email full report under NDA.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing supported; standard net-30 available for enterprise.
- Reserved capacity: 3-month minimum is fine for pilot; we’ll include an option to convert to a 6/12-month committed contract with stepped discounts in the SOW.
- NTE: if we set the pilot budget at $45k/month we’ll mark the SOW NTE at $135k for 3 months and include a sketch of the cost scenarios.

Action items from Redwood (owned):
- Rishi: upload final scenario tab to Drive + send calendar invite for 11am PT tomorrow.
- Monica: join call to talk latency sizing and fallback model behavior.
- Aditya: prepare a short note on how reserved capacity pricing works and the discount break-points for 3/6/12 month commits.

Links & attachments:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PulseCare-CostModel

I’ll follow up after the call with a finalized SOW and a one-page unit-econ summary (per-feature monthly cost, $/1M tokens, margin impact, and CAC payback sensitivity table).

Thanks — Rishi
